correctness.rationale: For the frozen RESULT.md lines 5–38, the centered linear coordinate x has squared norm S_n, path gradients 1 and closing gradient n−1. Its Rayleigh quotient is [B−(t−(n−1)^2)c]/S_n. The parabolic path weights solve Lx=Λx, and on monomials of degree k the scaled path operator is triangular with leading coefficient k(k+1)/2, so the path gap is simple and separated. Equality in Rayleigh at c=0 determines all weights by the vertex recurrences. The positive directional derivative at t<(n−1)^2 follows from the simple eigenvalue, decreasing each path weight uniformly while adding the chord. At equality Rayleigh attainment forces w_i=Λu_i−(n−1)c; positivity of L−ΛI on centered vectors is then equivalent to positivity of A_n−(c/Λ)((n−1)I−11^T) in difference coordinates. Indeed the squared norm of a centered cumulative sum has Gram entry C_ij=i(n−j)/n for i<=j; summing each row gives u_i. The constant gradient is a null vector; the smallest eigenvalue on its orthogonal complement gives precisely the claimed cutoff. The e_1 test yields ρ_n≤(n−1)/(2n)<1/2, so path weights remain strictly positive; a nonconstant null gradient appears at the endpoint. Independent exact characteristic polynomials confirm all four example radicals (python3 /tmp/opencode/frozen_math_reproduction.py).
